title: Retain server-authorized scope hardening for Collaboration comment edits
verify: The named editFieldComment action supplies server-resolved actor and target context to the existing Collaboration public boundary, which checks role, center/class/student membership, target ownership, and privacy before any write; URL lessonId mismatch alone does not deny an already authorized target.

A forged cross-center, cross-class, cross-student, or non-owned target returns 403 comment_forbidden, leaves the stored body and last-change timestamp unchanged, and does not disclose unrelated object existence.
An authorized owner edit of a permitted Collaboration target succeeds through the existing route action and Collaboration writer.

Source and runtime review prove that the route owns no direct Collaboration persistence, no alternate writer or mutation API is introduced, and the accepted Collaboration ownership and Lesson Context adapter boundary remain unchanged.
The focused isolated route/public-boundary proof is safe to rerun, records state before and after rejected and permitted edits, and never targets study-calendar.db.

evidence: Fresh independent verifier-owned route/public-boundary probe passed 1 file / 2 tests with class, lesson, selected-student scope, denial-before-mutation, same-context success, state snapshots, and cleanup.
Fresh verifier rerun recorded npm run check, npm run build, npm run test (78 files / 268 tests), git diff --check, mb-lint, and strict doctor PASS.

Fresh T3 semantic review passed 2/2 isolated tests and denied forged cross-lesson, cross-class, wrong-student, personal-to-shared-route, and other-author edits before mutation while preserving same-context success.
The semantic protocol contains exactly one SEMANTIC_VERDICT: semantic-pass and no material finding or operator question.

purpose: Retain the completed optional server-side authorization hardening from failed TASK-102 Attempt 3 without replaying the completed projection, named-action, or UI outcomes; the obsolete URL lesson-selector equality finding is not a current product defect.
success_outcome: The existing named editFieldComment action checks server-resolved role, center/class/student membership, target ownership, and privacy at the Collaboration write boundary: unauthorized cross-context edits fail before mutation, while an already authorized target remains permitted even when the URL lessonId differs.
anti_goals: Do not reopen, mutate, or inherit functional or semantic evidence from TASK-102-T3-FT-004-W35; its failed identity and Attempt 1-3 evidence remain historical.
Do not add a new top-level route, /api/lesson-context mutation endpoint, frontend state layer, SQLite schema, or persistence abstraction.

Do not trust client role, author, center, class, lesson, student, scope, or target claims as authority; the route context must be server-resolved and the Collaboration boundary must revalidate the stored target relationship.
Do not implement the Collaboration UI owned by TASK-103 or change unrelated FT-002, FT-005, FT-006, Identity & Access, Center & Scheduling, or Learning Progress behavior.
constraints: Keep the existing /lesson-context route and named editFieldComment action; pass only server-resolved actor/role/membership context and target selectors needed for authorization.
Keep Collaboration as the sole semantic writer and reuse its existing comment persistence and authorization path; no schema or API boundary change is planned.

Reject targets outside the actor's server-authorized center/class/student membership, ownership, or privacy scope before the UPDATE and preserve state-before/state-after equality for the denied target; URL lessonId mismatch alone is not a denial.
Use an isolated or disposable SQLite fixture for the route/public-boundary proof and never target study-calendar.db.
This is a fresh follow-up identity after TASK-102 exhausted its retry budget; do not run Attempt 4 or reuse TASK-102 evidence as current proof.
invariants: The authenticated actor and server-resolved role, center/class/student membership, target ownership, and privacy scope are part of the edit authorization decision.

A target outside the actor's authorized center/class/student or ownership scope is denied with the existing route failure envelope before body or timestamp mutation; a URL lessonId mismatch alone is not sufficient for denial.
An authorized owner editing a permitted target remains permitted.
Collaboration remains the only writer for field comments; Lesson Context remains a transport/composition adapter.
Denied cross-context edits do not reveal unrelated object existence and leave all relevant disposable state unchanged.
verification_targets: FT-004-AC-005 / REQ-014: forged or unauthorized center/class/student/ownership/privacy context cannot edit an otherwise owned comment; the denied request is non-mutating and does not disclose unrelated existence, while URL lessonId mismatch alone is not a negative case.

FT-004-AC-005 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/collaboration-browser-surface.md#authorized-mutation-transport: the named route action supplies current server-resolved context and the Collaboration public boundary validates target scope, actor, and ownership before writing.

.memory-bank/contracts/boundary-map.md#day-discussion-query-boundary and .memory-bank/architecture/system-architecture.md#composition-and-request-data-flow: the route delegates the edit to Collaboration without direct persistence or a second writer.

Claim-linked RED/GREEN isolated integration proof covers unauthorized cross-context denial, permitted owner success, state-before/state-after equality, safe rerun, cleanup, and all applicable native gates.

stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-redesign if satisfying the required role/membership/ownership/privacy authorization requires a new shared contract, new persistence schema, new mutation API, or a change to accepted Collaboration ownership.
Stop if the edit can be authorized only by trusting client authority fields or if the forged cross-context denial cannot be shown before mutation with state snapshots.
Stop if focused proof requires study-calendar.db, an existing server, destructive shared-state reset, or cleanup that is not failure-safe.
